title: Instrumented runbook task adaptor for telemetry-first self-heal
creator: Samir Patel
description: Create an adapter that converts existing runbooks into instrumented tasks that emit structured telemetry and can opt-in to automated self-heal actions. Goal is to make operational playbooks observable, testable, and safe to run automatically for common, low-risk incidents (e.g., stuck worker queues, transient model OOMs, cache thrash). Deliverables: 1) task adaptor library with a stable API, 2) telemetry schema and dashboard, 3) a gated self-heal engine with policy controls and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter library published to internal registry with semantic versioning and migration notes
Telemetry schema documented in Confluence and validated against 3 sample runbooks
Grafana dashboard showing runbook-invocation events, success/failure rates, and latency percentiles
Self-heal policies configurable per project and require dual-approval for high-risk actions
Integration test harness that replays recorded incidents and asserts expected automated actions
Audit trail persisted to KMS-backed storage with tenancy metadata

decisions: Opted for a small YAML DSL for runbook-to-task translation to lower barrier for SRE authors
Telemetry will be emitted to Kafka topic ops.runbooks.v1 with avro schema; Grafana will consume from materialized metrics in ClickHouse
Self-heal actions will have three risk tiers: 'safe' (auto), 'moderate' (auto with cooldown), 'dangerous' (manual only).
All automated actions require an audit entry and optional Slack notification in ops channel.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design & Security review (complete): spec + threat model
Phase 1 - Adapter alpha + sample conversions: internal infra and runtime teams
Phase 2 - Telemetry rollout: produce to staging topic, dashboard validation
Phase 3 - Self-heal gated beta: enable 'safe' actions for non-prod namespaces with observability
Phase 4 - Controlled prod enablement: gradual enablement by project with kill-switch and SLO guardrails
